a short code computed from the content, used to confirm a batch is the one that was approved

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and options
sections.what: Loads libraries and reads the command-line options for one industry, check-only mode, and the time budget.
sections.why: The header documents these options for running by hand and in setup.
sections.watch_out: The default time budget is 150 seconds; later batches wait for the next run.

sections.name: val, log, Outcome
sections.title: Logging and outcome record
sections.what: Defines the log helper and the record format used for each batch's result.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond its use in the report.
sections.watch_out: Unclear beyond the names; the record fields are what the report shows.

sections.name: pool
sections.title: Connection pool and run lock
sections.what: Opens a small connection pool and takes a lock that stops another replay from running at the same time, then loops over the industries.
sections.why: The lock prevents two replays from interleaving their writes.
sections.watch_out: The lock is held on one connection for the whole run, so it must be released or the next run will say another replay is running.

sections.name: stateOf
sections.title: Loaded state check
sections.what: Returns whether a given ledger batch is loaded, not loaded, partly loaded, or has nothing to load.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the function's comment, which says it is called by the run above.
sections.watch_out: A partly loaded result stops that industry, so a wrong state check blocks later batches.

sections.name: replayIndustry
sections.title: Replay for one industry
sections.what: Goes through the industry's batches in order, skips loaded ones, stops at partly loaded or mismatched batches, does a dry run and then a real load for matching ones, and writes the report.
sections.why: Stopping at the first problem stops later batches from loading out of order.
sections.watch_out: A mismatch blocks every later batch in that industry, so the report must be read before rerunning.

sections.name: importBatch
sections.title: Load one batch
sections.what: Runs the population importer directly, or runs the closure importer as a separate program and reads its report file.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the comment about the closure importer being a standalone script.
sections.watch_out: The closure path has a two-minute timeout and reads a fixed report path.

summary: Loads approved research batches into the database that are not loaded yet, checking each batch's plan fingerprint first, and stops an industry if a batch is partly loaded or does not match.
purpose: Brings the database up to date with approved research after a merge, without loading a batch twice or loading a batch that differs from what was approved.
why: The header says the setup should be safe to run at any time.
how: Takes a lock so only one run happens, reads each industry's ledger in order, and checks each batch's state. Pending batches get a dry run, and the fingerprint must match before a real load. Results go to a report file for each industry. Exit code is non-zero if anything was refused.
inputs: The replay ledger JSON files under data/yard-research, the DATABASE_URL setting, and command-line options for industry, check mode and time budget.
outputs: Console messages, a replay report JSON for each industry that loaded or refused something, and database rows when a batch is loaded.
risks: Writes many project rows. A stale ledger fingerprint blocks loads safely, but a wrong ledger entry would load the wrong data.
debug: Run with --check to see each batch's state. Read the replay-report.json for the industry, and compare the dry-run report against the approved report named in the ledger.
